Insignificant · presentation sandbox

The whole roster, fighting by its own numbers

Every unit class the game ships, at the era you pick, resolving attacks with the real catalog stats from core/data/cards.gd and the real roll order from core/battle.gd: accuracy, then dodge, with fortifications absorbing and engineers repairing them. Each fighter is one static sprite; all the motion is cheap transforms. This is a visualization sandbox for watching the numbers, not a proposal for the game's camera.

Real catalog stats

攻 and 血 come from the card catalog, multiplied by that era's cost coefficient (1/2/3/5/8/12). Switch era and every number rescales exactly as the game does.

source: cards.gd + era.gd

Accuracy, then dodge

Every strike rolls 命中率 first; a hit then rolls the target's 閃避率. Two separate rolls in that fixed order, mirroring Battle._fire. Misses and dodges are labelled on the field.

MISS · 閃避 · -N

Fortifications absorb

盾陣 eats one melee strike, 防空 eats one ranged or air strike, both ignoring attack value. With a living 工兵團 behind it the fort turns 待修 instead of being consumed.

格擋 · 修復

Siege and air demolish

火砲 (攻城) and 轟炸機 (空襲) skip the absorb rule entirely: while any enemy fortification stands they demolish it outright, with no roll and no repair.

no roll, no repair

攻速 sets cadence

A unit's 攻速 is attacks per 回合, so a 4.5-second demo round gives 攻速 1.4 a strike every 3.2s and 攻速 0.65 one every 6.9s. 工兵團 never attacks at all.

回合 = 4.5s

Static sprite, cheap motion

Each unit is a single PNG. Facing is an X flip, walking is a position tween, and liveliness is a sine bob. No walk-cycle frames exist, which is the point.

0 animation frames

What this is. A presentation sandbox for looking at units and their numbers. The top-down camera is a property of this sandbox and carries no implication for the game, whose battle screen is a locked side-view pair (design/戰鬥.md 場景呈現). A depandabot audit on 2026-07-25 falsified the case for a top-down game camera; see explore-topdown-battle-and-units.md.

Deliberate approximations (the numbers are the game's, the staging is not):

  • Continuous movement replaces the row model. core/battle.gd has no positions at all: a unit's only spatial attribute is a categorical row (melee / ranged / air). The columns and the walking here are invented by this view.
  • Nearest-enemy targeting replaces deploy-order focus fire. Core picks the first living defender in deploy order, preferring the melee row for melee attackers. This picks the nearest instead, keeping only the melee-row preference.
  • Both sides carry the quality triple. In the real game only player units roll 命中率 / 閃避率 / 攻速; every enemy fights at accuracy 100, dodge 0, speed 1.0 (battle.gd engine defaults). Here both sides use the medium-band midpoints so misses and dodges are visible on both teams.
  • Engineer repair is symmetric. Core grants the damaged-instead-of-consumed fort rule to the player side only; this gives it to whichever side has a living engineer.
  • One unit per class, one battle. No waves, no 軍費, no skill cards, no growth or medals, no difficulty scaling. Rolls use Math.random: determinism is the core's contract, not this sandbox's.
sprites: 52 exploratory top-down raws (256px, 128-colour, background keyed to transparent) from assets/exploration/topdown-demo/ · raws only, never pipeline assets.
exploratory prototype · view-layer only; the deterministic tick core is untouched.
